title: Pandas Data Cleaning: Revision Notes
summary: Quick revision notes on cleaning a pandas DataFrame: missing values, dtypes and conversion, duplicates, string methods, renaming, and apply versus vectorized operations.

chapters.title: Data Cleaning Mental Model
points: Cleaning means making every column the right dtype, with no hidden NaNs, no duplicate rows and consistent labels and text, before any analysis
Most pandas cleaning methods return a new object and leave the original untouched, so assign the result or the cleaning is lost
Work in a fixed order: inspect (info, describe, isna().sum()) → fix dtypes → handle missing → clean text and names → drop duplicates
df.info() shows dtype and non-null count per column; a text dtype (str in pandas 3, object in older pandas) on a numeric-looking column signals dirty data
Vectorized column operations run in compiled code across the whole column; row-by-row Python is the slow exception

chapters.title: Missing Values: isna, dropna, fillna
points: NaN, None and NaT all count as missing; isna() returns a boolean mask and notna() is its inverse
df.isna().sum() counts missing per column, and df.isna().mean() gives the fraction missing
dropna(): axis=0 drops rows, how='any' (default) vs how='all', subset=[cols] limits the check, thresh=n keeps rows with at least n non-null values
fillna(value) fills with a scalar or a per-column dict; df['a'].fillna(df['a'].median()) is the standard numeric fill; ffill() and bfill() fill from neighbours

Mistake: NaN == NaN is False, so df[df.a == np.nan] matches nothing; use isna(). Mistake: df['a'].fillna(x, inplace=True) on a column slice never changes df under pandas 3 Copy-on-Write, so assign df['a'] = df['a'].fillna(x)

chapters.title: Dtypes, Conversion and Duplicates
points: df.dtypes lists column types; a column with mixed values becomes object, and int columns turn float when NaN is present

astype('int64') and astype('datetime64[ns]') convert strictly and raise on bad values (astype('category') never raises: every value becomes a category); astype('Int64') (capital I) is the nullable integer that allows missing values
pd.to_numeric(s, errors='coerce') and pd.to_datetime(s, errors='coerce') turn unparseable values into NaN/NaT instead of raising; the default is errors='raise'
duplicated() marks repeat rows (keep='first' by default, so the first occurrence is False); drop_duplicates(subset=[cols], keep='first'|'last'|False) removes them, and keep=False drops every copy
Mistake: drop_duplicates() with no subset compares all columns, so near-duplicates differing in case or whitespace survive; clean text first, then dedupe

chapters.title: String Methods and Renaming
points: The .str accessor applies string methods to a whole Series: s.str.strip(), .lower(), .upper(), .title(), .len()
s.str.replace('old','new', regex=False) is a literal replace; regex=True uses patterns, e.g. s.str.replace(r'\s+',' ', regex=True) collapses whitespace
s.str.contains('x', na=False) gives a boolean filter mask, and .str.split(',', expand=True) splits into separate columns
Mistake: .str on a non-string column raises AttributeError, and missing values return NaN rather than erroring; convert first with astype('string')

df.rename(columns={'old':'new'}) renames chosen columns and returns a copy; df.columns = [...] replaces all names and must match the column count; rename(columns=str.lower) applies a function to every name

chapters.title: Apply vs Vectorized Operations
points: Vectorized operations such as df['a'] * 2, s.str.lower() or np.where(cond, x, y) run in compiled code across the whole column and are fastest
Series.apply(func) calls a Python function once per element; df.apply(func, axis=1) calls it once per row, which is the slowest pattern
Use apply only when no vectorized equivalent exists, such as multi-step custom logic; map(dict) is a fast lookup for value recoding
Replace row-wise if/else with np.where or boolean masks: df['tier'] = np.where(df.score >= 50, 'pass', 'fail')
Mistake: df.apply(f, axis=1) on a large frame is often 10 to 100 times slower than the vectorized form, and apply with the default axis=0 passes whole columns, not rows

chapters.title: Pandas Cleaning Cheat Sheet
points: Missing: isna().sum() → dropna(subset=, thresh=) or fillna(value | median) or ffill()
Types: info() / dtypes → astype('Int64'|'int64') strict; to_numeric / to_datetime(errors='coerce') lenient
Duplicates: duplicated().sum() to count → drop_duplicates(subset=[...], keep='first'|'last'|False)
Text and names: .str.strip().str.lower() → .str.replace(..., regex=False) → rename(columns={...}) or columns=str.lower
Speed order: vectorized ops and np.where first, map(dict) for lookups, apply(axis=1) last; always assign the result back
